name: Qualcomm
thesis: Qualcomm is a tracking-company value thesis, not a growth underwrite on the current evidence. The handset and QTL franchises still fund substantial cash returns, but Apple modem runoff, weak Android demand, memory and input-cost pressure, China exposure, and licensing or regulatory remedies leave the base case with anemic aggregate growth. The stock works first as a cheap-franchise value play; a durable re-rating requires automotive, industrial IoT and physical AI, PC and XR, and especially data center to outperform enough to more than replace declining handset and licensing economics while producing incremental EBIT and free cash flow. Treat management's long-range segment targets as options until disclosed revenue, mix, and margin conversion prove the new segments are carrying the company.
key_driver: Whether disclosed non-handset revenue and profit growth fully offset Apple, Android, and QTL erosion. The decisive signposts are non-handsets exceeding 50% of QCT in FY2027, data-center revenue converting toward the $5B FY2027 target, and automotive plus industrial IoT sustaining growth without further consolidated margin compression; absent those, QCOM remains only a value-supported tracking name.

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Green only when disclosed non-handset growth fully offsets handset and QTL erosion with positive incremental margin. Red if non-handsets remain below 45% of QCT by the second half of FY2027 or grow below 25% YoY for two quarters while the core declines.

nuance.bear_case: Qualcomm is a melting ice cube dressed as an AI story: its two profit engines are eroding in real time while management sells a data-center dream that produces little revenue before FY2028+. Apple is not a distant risk but an active run-off — management confirmed ~20% of iPhones in FY26 and ~0% in FY27 (Apple chip revenue from >$6B toward ~$2B), and Apple's 2019 QTL license expires ~April 2027, putting the highest-margin royalty stream on the table exactly as the chip relationship ends. The core is cracking today: QCT handset revenue is guided to collapse sequentially from ~$7.8B (Q1'26) to ~$4.9B (Q3'26 guide), QCT EBT margin has compressed from ~31% to a guided 25-27% on an ~89% LPDDR5X memory-cost spike, and ~46% of revenue rides on China, where OEMs are under-shipping and actively de-risking from US silicon. The celebrated >$15B FY29 data-center target rests on unshipped products (AI200 in 2026, AI250 sampling ~mid-2027, the Meta CPU a ~2028 part) in a market owned by NVIDIA (Rubin) and AMD (MI400) and attacked by the in-house silicon of the very hyperscalers QCOM must sell to (Meta MTIA, Google TPU, AWS Trainium) — and it is QCOM's third data-center attempt after Centriq (killed 2018) and Nuvia (redirected to laptops), with HBM supply largely pre-sold to incumbents. Management is funneling ~99% of FCF into buybacks to prop EPS while the earnings base is structurally impaired — the textbook value-trap tell — and the FY29 >$18 EPS / ~2x-revenue-by-2030 promises come from a team with a documented history of recycling multi-year diversification targets (the FY29 auto target was $8B at the 2024 Investor Day, now 'raised' to $10B).
nuance.adversarial_take: Bulls are extrapolating a pipeline into revenue and a product launch into market share — the two most reliable ways to lose money in semis. Every load-bearing bull number is a target, not a result: the $65B auto pipeline is design wins, not backlog; $15B data-center is products not in volume; >$14B IoT, ~$6B PC and >$18 EPS are all FY29. The '~$12.03 non-GAAP EPS / ~30% QCT margin' base is peak, not a run-rate to grow from — it embeds full Apple modem revenue (gone FY27), pre-crunch memory costs (now compressing QCT EBT to 25-27%), and an expired Huawei license. Most fundamentally, 'cheap on forward earnings' is being read as 'undervalued' when the correct read is that the forward multiple is low precisely because forward earnings are impaired and terminal value is uncertain — QCOM has promised 'diversification beyond handsets' for a decade (2021 Investor Day: TAM '$100B -> $700B') and the multiple has never re-rated because investors have seen this movie. The right posture is to want the business at a price that respects the Apple + China + margin trifecta and treats data-center/PC as free optionality — not to pay up for four FY29 targets at once. Where the bulls are genuinely right: automotive is real and converting (~$5B run-rate, +38% YoY, named OEM LOIs), QTL is a genuine ~72%-EBT annuity while it lasts, and strong FCF makes this a value-trap question, not a solvency one.
nuance.stress_test: If Apple modems go to ~0% in FY27 (-$4-5B revenue, management-confirmed) AND the ~April-2027 QTL renewal is lower or lapses (-$0.5-1.5B of ~72%-EBT royalty) AND the China/memory squeeze annualizes (QCT EBT 31% -> 25-27% across ~$32B QCT = ~$1.5-2B EBT lost) AND data-center contributes little in the window (~$0.3B FY26, even a hit-the-target $5B FY27 at commoditized ~20-25% EBT adds far less profit than the QTL/QCT dollars lost): revenue is roughly flat-to-down through FY27 while non-GAAP EPS falls from $12.03 toward ~$9-10 even with the ~99%-of-FCF buyback flattering per-share math. Put a de-rated ~11-13x on impaired ~$9.50 earnings (the multiple the market is already assigning) and the stock is ~$105-125 — roughly 30-40% downside from ~$176. The buyback is the only thing standing between reported EPS and a visible decline, which is exactly why it is ~99% of FCF: a crutch, not a capital-allocation triumph. The bull inverse: if auto compounds to $10B, the data-center ramp hits even ~$8-10B by FY29, and QTL renews, non-GAAP EPS approaches the >$18 target and an 18x-forward, ~7% FCF-yield entry re-rates violently toward peers.
nuance.valuation_whats_priced_in: At ~$176 / ~$186B market cap and ~18x forward / ~19x trailing / ~14.7x EV/EBITDA with a 2.1% dividend and ~6.8% FCF yield — the lowest forward multiple in the semi peer group and roughly in-line to slightly cheap on its own 10-yr median (~19.9x). The market prices in the durable QTL annuity, resilient Android handset, and the early auto/IoT ramp, and it prices in the bear (Apple insourcing, expired Huawei license, China/memory headwinds — hence the discount). It does NOT price in the data-center ramp to >$15B (treated as ~zero optionality since products are pre-volume), a successful PC share grab, or any multiple re-rate toward peers.
nuance.signposts_trap_vs_turn: TURN signals: fiscal Q4'26/Q1'27 handset recovering above ~$6B with QCT EBT back toward ~29-30% (the memory/China trough was cyclical, not structural); first real data-center revenue disclosure tracking the $0.3B->$5B FY27 ramp (AI200 volume, AI250 on time); Apple QTL renewed on flat-or-better terms; auto converting the $65B pipeline toward the $6B exit run-rate. TRAP signals: handset staying below ~$5B with EBT stuck at 25-27% (structural erosion); data-center revenue materially below ~$3-4B run-rate by mid-FY27 (AI200 slips / AI250 sampling delayed); QTL guided below ~$5B FY27 or the Apple renewal announced worse/absent; new China royalty-rate concession or 6G licensing litigation; buyback pace masking a visible EPS decline.
nuance.watch_mgmt_qa: Track how management handles the hard questions on the earnings Q&A rather than the prepared remarks: (1) the exact Apple modem/QTL run-off cadence and whether they will confirm or dodge the ~April-2027 license status; (2) concrete data-center revenue recognition timing and named hyperscaler commitments beyond Meta/HUMAIN (vs. reiterating the FY29 target); (3) whether QCT handset EBT margin recovers post-trough or they hedge on memory costs; (4) how they frame the $65B auto 'pipeline' vs. recognized backlog when pressed on conversion.

competitive_watchlist: Apple (in-house C1/C2/C3 modems — the direct handset + RF displacement)
MediaTek (Android SoC share, especially China / lower tiers)
NVIDIA (data-center Rubin + auto Drive Thor — the frontier QCOM must attack)
Hyperscaler in-house silicon (Meta MTIA, Google TPU, AWS Trainium)
thesis_breakers_qualitative: Apple modem run-off deeper/faster than the ~$7-8B FY27 base — confirmed ~0% of iPhones FY27 — AND it poisons the ~April-2027 QTL renewal (a chip-less Apple has less reason to accept QCOM's royalty terms).

The >$15B FY29 data-center target proving fiction: AI200 volume slips, AI250 sampling delays past mid-2027, or the Meta/HUMAIN commitments do not convert to disclosed revenue — the entire re-rating leg breaks (attempt #3 after Centriq/Nuvia).
QCOM's data-center customers (Meta/Google/AWS) accelerating in-house silicon while NVIDIA/AMD own the frontier and pre-committed HBM supply locks QCOM out of the scarce input.
QTL confirmed a decaying annuity: China royalty-rate pressure, device-ASP cap dynamics, 6G licensing disputes, or the Apple April-2027 cliff pulling QTL revenue below ~$5B FY27.
~46% China concentration realized as a tail risk: export-control escalation or accelerated Chinese silicon substitution hitting nearly half the business.
Sustained margin compression: QCT EBT stuck at 25-27% (or lower) and GAAP operating margin below ~22% on memory-cost inflation and Apple/China mix loss, rather than recovering post-trough.

The $65B auto 'pipeline' failing to convert: design-win-to-revenue slippage, auto cyclicality, or NVIDIA Drive / Mobileye / OEM in-sourcing capping the run-rate short of the $10B FY29 target (itself a raised recycle of the prior $8B).
Buyback-as-crutch exposed: ~99% of FCF into repurchases masking a shrinking earnings base, with the FY29 >$18 EPS / ~2x-revenue targets missed like prior multi-year promises.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction; for QCOM this is the direct read that non-handset growth is failing to outrun the Apple + China/memory handset run-off.
GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — operating loss.
Gross margin below 20% for 2 consecutive quarters — severe pricing/cost issue. (Universal floor; the per-ticker rule below is stricter.)

business_model_rules.narrative: QCOM is a fabless, high-margin semi + IP-licensing hybrid that has run GAAP operating margin around ~26% (QTL ~72% EBT, QCT ~25-31% EBT); operating margin sustained below 22% for two quarters means memory-cost inflation (LPDDR +89% in Q2'26) and adverse mix (Apple modem loss, China under-shipping) have overwhelmed the structural margin advantage — the core cash engine eroding faster than diversification can offset.

QCOM blended GAAP gross margin runs ~56% on the QTL licensing lift plus QCT chipset margin; sustained gross margin below 50% for two quarters signals either QTL (the ~72%-margin annuity) shrinking as a share of mix or chipset pricing/cost pressure — a direct hit to the thesis's high-margin core.

The bull case leans on ~$12.8B FCF (~29% margin) funding the ~99%-of-FCF buyback that anchors per-share EPS through the Apple transition; FCF margin below 18% for two quarters means cash conversion is eroding and the buyback crutch loses its funding just as the earnings base is under structural pressure.
